title: The Kingdom Splits
reflectionText: Rehoboam rejected the counsel to serve the people and answered them roughly. Israel broke away, and the word Yahweh had spoken through Ahijah was fulfilled. A harsh answer became the moment an already-promised division took shape. What changes when leadership chooses service instead of force?
editorialNotes: PAL Daily supervised production 2026-07-24, Batch D (gap CG11). 1 Kings 12, Rehoboam and the division of the kingdom, absent both lanes; opens the divided-monarchy era. SHORT + FULL, WEB 303/524w, KJV 329/602w. SHORT covers the confrontation and split (12:1-20, ending on 'only the tribe of Judah followed David's house'); FULL runs to the chapter close (adds the averted civil war and Shemaiah's word, 12:21-24, and Jeroboam's two golden calves at Bethel and Dan, 12:25-30 — 'behold your gods, O Israel'). The two counsels and the 'whips/scorpions' answer are kept as essential dialogue; the narrator notes, as the text does, that 'the cause was from Yahweh/the LORD' (12:15). WEB uses 'Yahweh', KJV 'the LORD'. New character rehoboam added to character_registry. Narrator/mood/length were authoring selections (title/anchor owner-given) — flagged for owner review.
